summary: An inter-State co-operative society that works in more than one State can apply to the Registrar to become a Producer Company. To do this, it must submit a special resolution from at least two-thirds of its members, along with required statements and a correct declaration. Once the Registrar approves and issues a certificate, the society officially transforms into a Producer Company.
points: An inter-State co-operative society with objects not limited to one State may apply to the Registrar to register as a Producer Company.
The application must include a special resolution passed by at least two-thirds of the total members of the society.
The application must include details of directors, the Chief Executive, the list of members, and a statement showing its objects.
Two or more directors must declare in writing that all the provided details are correct.
Upon successful registration, the words Producer Company Limited must be added to the end of the company's name.
After registration, the old co-operative society transforms into a Producer Company and is governed strictly by this Chapter.
example: Greenfields Agro Inter-State Co-operative Society operated farming and trade activities across two different states. The leaders and members decided it would be better to change their legal form. They held a meeting where a special resolution was passed by two-thirds of all their total members to incorporate as a Producer Company. Two of the directors signed a formal declaration stating that all the names, addresses, lists of members, and object statements were completely correct. They submitted this application to the Registrar along with the required documents. After reviewing everything, the Registrar certified the registration. Greenfields Agro Inter-State Co-operative Society officially became Greenfields Agro Producer Company Limited and started operating under the new law.

terms.meaning: A co-operative society whose objects and activities are not confined to just one State.
A formal decision passed by a high majority of at least two-thirds of the total members.
The official government authority responsible for registering companies.

watch: Make sure to note that at least two-thirds of the total members must agree via a special resolution before applying.
